rules.statement: Keep `*.Abstractions` packages to contracts only; put any type that carries behavior (parsing, hashing, member production) in a separate logic-bearing package that the abstractions packages may reference.
rules.why: Abstractions packages contain contracts only, no logic; referencing a model library is fine because the logic then doesn't live in the abstractions package.
rules.check: Look for method bodies with real logic, static helpers or behavior-bearing classes added to a project named `*.Abstractions`.

rules.statement: In a DI-free library, don't add a static mutable registry for an open vocabulary; ship the standard entries as built-in data and take any other entry from the caller as an argument or overload.
rules.why: A static mutable registry is global state with registration-order and test-isolation problems, and a DI-free package cannot reach a DI registry.
rules.check: Look for static mutable collections, `Register(...)` methods or static `Add` APIs that let callers extend a vocabulary globally in a package without dependency injection.

rules.statement: Model an open vocabulary as names plus sealed registered data, with the standard entries built in and found through a `TryGet`-style lookup, rather than a closed enum or a per-type converter hierarchy.
rules.why: Per the open-vocabulary decision, an open vocabulary is names plus registered data, so contributed entries work with no library change.
rules.check: Look for new enums or switch statements over a vocabulary that is defined by an extensible registry (IANA or similar), or abstract per-entry classes where a sealed data descriptor would do.

rules.statement: Don't derive a registry name or trait from another identifier by string rewriting (for example lowercasing `HashAlgorithmName.Name`); map each known name explicitly and fail for unknown ones instead of guessing.
rules.why: No trait is inferred from a name; a name that doesn't match the registry must fail rather than be guessed.
rules.check: Look for `ToLowerInvariant`, `Replace` or similar transforms that turn one identifier (algorithm name, enum name) into a registry or wire name.

rules.statement: Validate a set of caller-supplied descriptors as a whole: throw `ArgumentException` for a null entry or for two descriptors with the same name.
rules.why: Descriptors are validated as a whole, like the key type catalog, so a duplicate or null entry never silently wins or crashes later.
rules.check: Look for constructors or methods taking `IEnumerable<...Descriptor>` that build a lookup without rejecting null entries or duplicate names (e.g., using indexer assignment that overwrites).

rules.statement: Let a constructor adopt an already in-memory value (`JsonElement`, `JsonObject`, a collection) and reserve a static `Parse(string)` for reading text.
rules.why: The decision separates adopting an in-memory value (constructor) from reading text (Parse).
rules.check: Look for constructors that take a JSON string and parse it, or `Parse` methods that take an already-parsed value.

rules.statement: Back an immutable JSON-wrapping type with a detached `JsonElement` that owns no `JsonDocument`, so it needs no disposal or defensive cloning.
rules.why: A detached immutable element leaves nothing to dispose or defensively clone.
rules.check: Look for wrapper types that hold a `JsonDocument` field, implement `IDisposable` only to free it, or clone on every access.

rules.statement: When computing an RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint, always include `kty` in the required members and order members ordinally.
rules.why: RFC 7638 §3.2 requires `kty` among the thumbprint members and §3.3 requires lexicographic (ordinal) member order.
rules.check: Check thumbprint member lists and canonicalization code: `kty` must be present, and sorting must use ordinal comparison, not culture-sensitive comparison.

rules.statement: Detect JWK private key material fail-closed: always treat the standard private member names (`d`, `p`, `q`, `dp`, `dq`, `qi`, `oth`, `k`, `priv`) as private in addition to any key-type-specific private members.
rules.why: A contributed key type must not be able to declare a standard private name public, so an RSA key carrying `k` is still rejected.
rules.check: Look for private-member checks or public-key projections that rely only on a per-key-type list and could let a standard private member through.

rules.statement: Produce JWK Thumbprint URIs only with whole-digest hash names; never emit truncated registry names such as `sha-256-128`.
rules.why: An RFC 7638 thumbprint is the whole digest, and a truncated key identifier weakens the binding.
rules.check: Look for hash-name maps or thumbprint URI code that includes truncated Named Information registry entries or truncates the digest.

rules.statement: Validate a caller-supplied Named Information hash name against the RFC 6920 §3 `alg` rule (`1*unreserved`), and for a hash with a known registry name require exactly that name.
rules.why: The open overload must accept unknown registered names but must never mislabel a known hash.
rules.check: Look for thumbprint URI or `ni:` URI code that accepts a hash name without checking unreserved characters or without checking it against the known mapping for that algorithm.

rules.statement: When reading a JWK Set, skip a key whose `kty` is missing, not a string or empty, using the same test the single-key reader applies, rather than failing the whole set.
rules.why: One malformed key must never poison the set.
rules.check: Look for JWKS parsing that throws on one bad key, or that uses a different `kty` validity test than the single-key type.
